scams.name: Sanur-Nusa Penida Fast Boat Ticket Overcharge & Fake-Operator Fraud
scams.description: Nusa Penida has surged from day-trip-only Bali side attraction to major 2025 destination — and the Sanur-Penida fast-boat market is now one of Bali's most-scammed tourist transits. Community reports document the operator-quality landscape and safety concerns; smaller vessels and less-regulated operators have documented capsizing incidents in rough seas. The 2025 scams: (a) pier-front touts at Sanur Beach selling 'fast boat Nusa Penida Rp 350K-500K' when the real rate via operator direct is Rp 125K–175K one-way (US$8–$11); (b) fake-operator websites spoofing 'Maruti Group Express' or 'Angel Billabong' with lookalike URLs selling non-existent tickets; (c) bundled 'day tour' packages starting at Rp 400K that secretly exclude the return boat, leaving tourists stranded to buy a Rp 400K 'emergency return'; (d) 'VIP front-row seat upgrade Rp 200K' at pier check-in — all seats are identical on these boats; (e) tourists told 'regular boat cancelled, only VIP available' when all boats run the same 30-min schedule. Community reports document the legitimate operator landscape. For older travelers: (1) book fast-boat tickets ONLY via Klook, 12go Asia, or the operator's direct website (Maruti Group Express, Angel Billabong Fast Cruise, El Rey Fast Cruise, Arjuna Express) at Rp 125K–175K one-way; (2) book return at the same time as outbound to lock rate and seat; (3) PRINT your ticket AND have PDF on phone — pier verification is chaotic; (4) NEVER buy from walk-up touts or WhatsApp-only sellers; (5) check sea conditions before departure — fast boats to Penida cancel 5–10% of days in Oct–Mar wet season; (6) arrive at Sanur pier 45 min before departure (no assigned seats, first-come first-served on open-seating boats); (7) for older travelers with balance concerns, request front-row or rear-row (middle rows bounce hardest); (8) bring seasickness meds (Promag or Dramamine); the 30–45 min crossing can be rough.
scams.avoidance: Book via Klook, 12go Asia, or operator direct (Maruti Group, Angel Billabong, El Rey) Book return at the same time as outbound — Rp 125K–175K one-way PRINT ticket AND save PDF; NEVER buy from walk-up touts Check sea conditions; arrive at Sanur pier 45 min early Bring seasickness meds; request front/rear seat if balance-sensitive
scams.location: Sanur Beach harbour (Bali departure), Serangan fast-boat pier, Toyapakeh/Banjar Nyuh/Sampalan ports (Nusa Penida arrival), online fake-operator sites

scams.name: Kelingking Beach / Broken Beach / Angel Billabong 'Park Fee' Padding & Parking Touts
scams.description: Nusa Penida's iconic west-coast viewpoints (Kelingking Beach, Broken Beach, Angel's Billabong, Crystal Bay) host a 2025 'entry fee' and parking-tout scam ecosystem that's become the island's second-biggest tourist complaint after boat transfers. Community threads on the pricing-controversy question. The legitimate fee structure: a SINGLE 'conservation fee' of Rp 25,000 (US$1.50) per foreign visitor, collected at the Toyapakeh port OR at the first viewpoint entered, valid for the whole day — covers Kelingking, Broken Beach, Angel Billabong, Atuh Beach, and Diamond Beach together. The 2025 scams: (a) 'additional Rp 50K per viewpoint' charged at each successive stop — tourists are told the port fee 'doesn't cover this one'; the real policy is one fee covers all official viewpoints; (b) parking-attendant 'fees' at Rp 25K–50K per stop at UNOFFICIAL 'parking areas' near the real entrances — scammers with reflective vests directing traffic to their own car-park commission ring; (c) 'mandatory local guide Rp 200K' at Kelingking viewpoint trail head — no guide is required; the 400-step descent is self-service; (d) 'toilet fee Rp 20K' at remote viewpoints (Rp 5K is legitimate); (e) combo-ticket sellers at the Toyapakeh port selling 'all-access pass Rp 150K' for the single Rp 25K pass. Community reports document the broader Nusa Penida pricing inflation. For older travelers: (1) pay the single Rp 25K conservation fee ONCE at Toyapakeh port or first viewpoint — keep the receipt; show it at each subsequent stop to refuse duplicate fees; (2) REFUSE every 'additional fee' at successive viewpoints — the single port fee is the whole island access; (3) for parking, park at the OFFICIAL entrance (look for a kiosk with printed rates) — fee is Rp 5K for motorbike, Rp 10K for car; reject any 'attendant' in a reflective vest directing you to an unofficial lot; (4) no guide is required at Kelingking — the 400-step descent is strenuous; older travelers should view from the top rim only (iconic T-Rex shape viewpoint); (5) bring small-bill rupiah (Rp 10K, 25K, 50K) to pay exact amounts and refuse 'no change' pressure; (6) for older travelers with mobility concerns, SKIP Kelingking Beach descent (400 steps each way) — photo from top rim is sufficient; (7) Diamond Beach also has steep steps (180+); Crystal Bay is the most accessible.
scams.avoidance: Pay ONE Rp 25K conservation fee at Toyapakeh; keep receipt, show each stop REFUSE every 'additional fee' claim at subsequent viewpoints Park at OFFICIAL kiosks with printed rates: Rp 5–10K only No guide is required anywhere; refuse Rp 200K 'mandatory' claims Bring small-bill rupiah (10K, 25K, 50K) to counter 'no change' pressure
scams.location: Kelingking Beach viewpoint parking, Broken Beach (Pasih Uug) entrance, Angel's Billabong tidal pool parking, Crystal Bay approach

scams.name: Nusa Penida Scooter Rental + Dangerous Road Conditions (Injury Scam)
scams.description: Nusa Penida's road network is among the most hazardous in Bali province — narrow, steep, potholed, and full of blind curves — and the island's scooter-rental ecosystem hosts a 2025 scam layered on genuine danger. Community threads document the accident rate and rental logistics consistently across 2024–2025. The 2025 scams and risks: (a) pre-damage fraud — unphotographed scratches claimed as 'tourist damage' at return, Rp 1M–3M demanded; (b) poorly-maintained scooters with brake wear, bald tyres, or broken speedometers rented at same rates as good units; (c) 'crash repair' demands Rp 3M–8M for minor scratches caused by the scooter's pre-existing brake failure; (d) rural 'helpful local' scam where a friendly stranger appears after a crash, offers to 'call the owner', then quotes Rp 5M+ 'repair cost' that's split as kickback; (e) real accident rate: hospital records at Bali Mandara (ambulance transfer from Penida) suggest 5–10 foreigner scooter-accidents per week in peak season, some requiring evacuation to Bali. Community warnings consistently flag the Nusa Penida scooter risk. For older travelers — or anyone without STRONG scooter experience — DO NOT rent a scooter in Nusa Penida. Hire a driver-plus-car (Toyota Avanza type) for the day at Rp 600K–900K (US$40–$60) — split between 2–4 people this is cheap and zero-risk. If you still choose to rent: (1) ONLY rent through your hotel or a Google 4.7+ operator with written rental agreement; (2) photo and video EVERY scratch before signing; keep your own photos; (3) test the brakes, horn, speedometer BEFORE leaving the rental; refuse any scooter with visible brake wear; (4) wear a helmet (no exceptions) and closed-toe shoes; (5) avoid the Kelingking approach road in rain — steep, loose surface; (6) DO NOT ride after sunset — no road lighting, animals on road; (7) if you crash, call your hotel's manager FIRST before engaging any roadside 'helper'; (8) purchase travel insurance with motorbike coverage (most don't include scooter by default); helicopter transfer to Bali is Rp 20M–40M if required.
scams.avoidance: DON'T rent a scooter — hire driver-plus-car at Rp 600–900K per day If renting, use hotel or Google 4.7+ shop; test brakes before leaving Photo/video EVERY scratch BEFORE signing NEVER ride after sunset; avoid rainy Kelingking approach road Purchase travel insurance WITH motorbike coverage (most exclude by default)
scams.location: Toyapakeh/Sampalan scooter rental shacks, Banjar Nyuh port-adjacent rentals, Kelingking approach road, Diamond Beach trail, rural Penida interior roads

scams.name: Full-Day Driver Tour Commission Stops & Kickback Upcharging
scams.description: The 'full-day private driver tour' is Nusa Penida's safest and best transport option for older travelers — but it also hosts a 2025 commission-stops ecosystem. Community reports cover the driver-hire landscape and the specific cost-value trade-off. The legitimate fare for a full-day driver with Toyota Avanza (4 passengers + luggage) is Rp 600K–900K (US$40–$60) for 8–10 hours covering the West Coast circuit (Kelingking, Broken Beach, Angel Billabong, Crystal Bay) or East Coast circuit (Diamond Beach, Atuh, Tree House, Suwehan). The 2025 scams: (a) port-front drivers quoting 'Rp 1.5M–2M day tour' and padding with secret commission stops (artisan shops, 'herbal medicine', batik showrooms); (b) 'must-visit cultural center' stops that eat 1–2 hours of actual sightseeing; (c) 'lunch at my friend's restaurant' where the menu is 2–3x normal prices and the driver gets 30% kickback; (d) 'sunset viewing ticket Rp 100K per person' at viewpoints that are free; (e) last-minute 'return port fee' demand of Rp 100K at tour end. Community reports cover itinerary planning for Nusa Penida and Lembongan. For older travelers: (1) book the driver via your hotel at Rp 600K–900K for the day (specify circuit in writing: West Coast OR East Coast — doing both in one day is rushed and exhausting); (2) CONFIRM in writing: start time, end time, stops list, lunch responsibility (whose choice), and NO shop detours; (3) pay 30% deposit; balance at tour end; (4) if driver attempts an unplanned 'shop stop', firmly say 'tidak, terima kasih — langsung saja' (no thanks, direct please); (5) for lunch, choose yourself from Google reviews (Penida Colada, Amok Resto, Warung D'Lods) and eat on YOUR schedule; (6) refuse every 'sunset viewing ticket' and 'extra fee' — it's included in the day rate; (7) for older travelers with mobility concerns, tell the driver explicitly which viewpoints require stair descents (Kelingking 400 steps, Diamond 180 steps) — you can view from top-rim parking for most; (8) tip Rp 50–100K for good service at tour end (not obligatory but kind).
scams.avoidance: Book via hotel at Rp 600K–900K for the day; specify circuit in writing CONFIRM stops list, lunch arrangement, and no shop detours in advance Say 'tidak, terima kasih — langsung saja' to unplanned shop stops Choose lunch yourself via Google 4.5+ warungs on YOUR schedule Refuse ALL 'extra fee' claims at tour end; day rate includes everything
scams.location: Toyapakeh port driver-tout zone, Penida Hotel / guesthouse booking arrangements, Kelingking/Diamond Beach circuit drive, Crystal Bay approach

scams.name: Nusa Penida ATM Scarcity & Hotel Cash-Exchange Padding
scams.description: Nusa Penida's banking infrastructure is significantly thinner than Bali proper — only 6–8 ATMs on the entire island (~200 km²), all in Toyapakeh and Sampalan towns. This scarcity is exploited by a 2025 cash-shortage ecosystem. Community reports document the overall cost inflation on Penida, with cash-management planning guidance noting the daily cash burn rate is higher than most visitors expect. The 2025 scams: (a) Toyapakeh port ATMs are freestanding (not bank-branch) and skimmer-vulnerable — same Bali 2025 card-skimming pattern documented across community reports; (b) hotel reception 'emergency cash exchange' at Rp 17,000 per USD when Bank Indonesia rate is Rp 15,800 (8% padding); (c) 'no ATM working island-wide' cover story used by hotels/guesthouses to push tourists toward padded exchange; (d) credit-card surcharge fraud where hotels add 5–8% 'credit card processing fee' not disclosed at check-in; (e) restaurant cash-only policies at tourist-zone warungs with inflated menu vs walk-in locals. Community planning guidance for getting around Penida is consistently documented. For older travelers: (1) BRING Rp 2M–4M (US$125–$250) cash from Bali BEFORE the fast-boat — exchange at PT Central Kuta Money Changer at the Sanur exchange kiosk (verified 4.6+ Google); (2) withdraw cash ONLY at ATMs INSIDE bank branches in Toyapakeh or Sampalan during business hours (8 AM–4 PM Mon–Fri) — BCA and Mandiri have branches; (3) REFUSE hotel cash exchange above 2% below Bank Indonesia rate (check bi.go.id daily); (4) CONFIRM credit-card surcharge policy at check-in (it should be 0–3% max, disclosed upfront); (5) budget Rp 400K–800K per day per person for food, transport, entry fees — carry slightly more for emergencies; (6) use bank-app transaction alerts for any Penida purchases; (7) have one dedicated travel debit card separate from main account; (8) if stranded with card issues, Sanur-Penida fast-boats run until 5 PM — you can return to Bali same-day for banking access.
scams.avoidance: BRING Rp 2M–4M cash from Bali BEFORE boarding the fast-boat Use ONLY bank-branch ATMs in Toyapakeh/Sampalan (BCA, Mandiri, business hours) Refuse hotel exchange above 2% below Bank Indonesia rate (bi.go.id) Confirm credit-card surcharge at check-in (should be 0–3% max) Budget Rp 400K–800K per day per person; carry buffer for emergencies
scams.location: Toyapakeh port ATM kiosks, Sampalan town ATMs (few and overnight-risky), Penida hotel reception cash desks, guesthouse currency exchange

scams.name: Nusa Penida Manta Point Snorkel Tour Unlicensed Boat Safety Scam
scams.description: Nusa Penida's snorkelling circuit (Manta Point, Crystal Bay, Gamat Bay, Toyapakeh) is one of Bali province's top marine experiences — but hosts a 2025 unlicensed-operator and safety-compromise ecosystem. Community reports document the operator quality variance, and snorkel-guide threads give practical venue information. The legitimate snorkel trip: 3–4 hour tour covering 4 sites, mask/snorkel/fins/life-jacket provided, boat with VHF radio and first-aid, at Rp 350K–550K (US$22–$35) per person group tour. The 2025 scams: (a) pier-front touts at Toyapakeh selling 'private Manta boat Rp 1.8M' when group tour at Rp 400K covers the same sites; (b) unlicensed operators without life jackets, VHF radio, or emergency equipment — serious in Manta Point open-water conditions; (c) rushed tours that skip Manta Point 'due to bad conditions' but charge full price and still hit the easier Crystal/Gamat sites only (check weather independently); (d) gear-rental inflation where mask/snorkel/fins 'premium set Rp 150K' when operator-provided gear is included; (e) 'manta sighting guarantee Rp 200K surcharge' — no operator can guarantee wildlife; (f) boats overloaded 20+ passengers past legal capacity. Community reviews consistently raise both the tour-value trade-off and the safety-quality variance. For older travelers — Manta Point is open ocean and can have 1–2m swells; if not a strong swimmer, skip Manta and do Crystal Bay only (protected): (1) book through your hotel or reputable operators (Sunshine Bali Tour, D'Camel Fast Cruise, Freebird Experience) at Rp 350K–550K per person group tour; (2) VERIFY life jackets for every passenger BEFORE boarding; (3) VERIFY boat has VHF radio and first-aid kit visible; (4) ask the guide to explain the current and wind conditions before Manta Point; (5) use YOUR OWN mask and snorkel if you have them — rental gear hygiene is variable; (6) skip the 'manta sighting guarantee' — mantas are seasonal (best May–Oct) and depend on conditions; (7) for older travelers with heart or breathing conditions, Crystal Bay only is sufficient — Manta Point requires treading water in deep open ocean; (8) check reviewed operator safety records on Google — avoid operators without clear reviews or with recent accident mentions.
scams.avoidance: Book via hotel or Sunshine Bali Tour / D'Camel / Freebird at Rp 350K–550K group VERIFY life jackets and VHF radio BEFORE boarding Skip Manta Point if not strong swimmer — Crystal Bay only (protected) Refuse 'manta sighting guarantee' — mantas are seasonal (May–Oct) Check Google reviews; avoid operators with recent accident mentions
scams.location: Toyapakeh port snorkel boat launches, Crystal Bay (west coast), Manta Point (south coast open water), Gamat Bay snorkel sites
